what_happened: The job "Open the job's PR early at verification start so CI caches during verify" (20261025-070538-8ra0) failed at admission. Admission refused the change because crates/athena-core/src/gh.rs adds an email address outside the allow-list. The event lists no unmet acceptance criteria, no blocker or major findings and no failed checks. The code was written, but it was refused before verification, so nothing landed.
cause: Admission enforces an email allow-list, but neither the reading, the plan nor the producer prompt shows that list or says email literals are restricted. Nothing scans the diff for emails before the job is submitted for admission. A job that opens a PR needs a commit or bot identity, and the natural way to supply one is a literal in gh.rs. So the rule is found only at the end. This is the same kind of gap as the banned-word case, which is caught only by a late test. The class is separate because the rule here is a diff-level admission check on email addresses.
prevention: Run the admission email allow-list scan on the working diff inside the producer loop, as a required check, so a disallowed address fails the producer's own run with the file and line. Also put the allow-list rule in the producer prompt: identities come from config or git settings, never from literals in code.
proposed_request: Open the job's pull request early, at the start of verification, so CI runs and caches while the verifier works. Outcome: during verification the PR is already open on the host, and the later landing still works. Do not write any email address into source files. If an identity is needed, take it from existing config or git settings, or use an address already on the admission allow-list. Before finishing, run the admission email allow-list check on your diff and make sure it passes. Existing tests must still pass.
